answer: Bind each agent identity to a unique hardware enclave attestation, like a quartz crystal with a one-of-a-kind resonance: the enclave signs every action with a key that cannot be copied to another machine, so one device yields exactly one identity. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand devices, turning a cheap software trick into an umber-heavy hardware bill. Identities that misbehave lose their attestation, and the saffron-priced device behind it becomes worthless to the network, so fraud scales with real cost instead of copy-paste.
